strikes.title: FBI Says North Korean Hackers Stole Over $400 Million in Crypto Using Deepfake Video Calls
strikes.location: United States (victims worldwide)
strikes.data_affected: Cryptocurrency funds and executive identity (voice/face)
strikes.impact: Over $400 million in crypto stolen from exchanges and funds via social engineering.
strikes.prevention: Verify high-value transfer requests out-of-band, require dual authorization, and train staff to treat unexpected video calls as untrusted.
strikes.summary: State-backed operators impersonated executives on deepfake video calls to trick employees into approving fraudulent cryptocurrency transfers worth hundreds of millions of dollars.

strikes.title: SilentAir Hijacks Asian Telecom Networks to Intercept SMS 2FA Codes and Spy on Taiwanese Users
strikes.location: Taiwan
strikes.data_affected: SMS one-time codes, 2FA tokens and private communications
strikes.impact: Telecom networks hijacked to intercept 2FA codes and spy on targeted Taiwanese users.
strikes.prevention: Replace SMS 2FA with phishing-resistant (FIDO2) MFA, and harden and monitor signalling (SS7/Diameter) interconnects.
strikes.summary: A stealthy group compromised telecom infrastructure to intercept SMS one-time codes, defeating 2FA and enabling surveillance of targeted users.

strikes.title: Operation Endgame Takes Down Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC Servers, Seizes 6.4M Stolen Logins
strikes.location: Europe (coordinated takedown)
strikes.data_affected: 6.4 million stolen logins and session tokens
strikes.impact: Info-stealer botnets (Gootloader, CastleRAT, StealC) seized; 6.4M credentials recovered.
strikes.prevention: Rotate credentials exposed to info-stealers, enforce MFA everywhere, and block execution of unsigned loaders on endpoints.
strikes.summary: An international law-enforcement operation dismantled malware infrastructure and recovered millions of stolen credentials harvested by info-stealers.

strikes.title: Trezor Confirms Hidden Implants in CryptoBilis-Sold Wallets That Can Steal Recovery Phrases
strikes.location: Czechia (global customers)
strikes.data_affected: Cryptocurrency wallet recovery phrases / private keys
strikes.impact: Resold hardware wallets carried implants able to steal recovery phrases and drain funds.
strikes.prevention: Buy hardware wallets only from the vendor or authorised sellers, and verify tamper-evidence and firmware signatures before first use.
strikes.summary: Tampered hardware wallets sold through a third-party reseller contained hidden implants capable of exfiltrating users' recovery phrases.

strikes.title: How Fake Job Interviews Helped Hackers Pull Off a $6.3 Billion Crypto Heist
strikes.location: United Arab Emirates (global crypto firms)
strikes.data_affected: Developer workstations, signing keys and cryptocurrency funds
strikes.impact: Fake-recruiter malware led to a multi-billion-dollar cryptocurrency heist.
strikes.prevention: Verify recruiters and candidates out-of-band, run coding tasks only in isolated throwaway VMs, and protect signing keys with hardware and multi-signature.
strikes.summary: Operatives used fake job interviews and malicious coding tasks to plant malware on developers at crypto firms, enabling one of the largest cryptocurrency thefts on record.

strikes.title: Cursor Says Stolen Fireworks AI Key Led to Trojanized Claude Code Extension Incident
strikes.location: Cursor's extension marketplace (Cursor Inc., US-based); breach originated via Fireworks AI, also US-based.
strikes.data_affected: Cursor-issued API/access key exposed at Fireworks AI; data copied from Cursor's read-only systems; Anthropic's official Claude Code extension on Cursor's marketplace was trojanized.
strikes.impact: Users of Cursor's extension marketplace who downloaded or used the compromised Claude Code extension were potentially exposed to a trojanized tool; the full scale of affected users was not disclosed in the report.
strikes.prevention: Implement short-lived, scoped API keys with automatic rotation and revocation monitoring, ensuring that a third-party vendor breach cannot expose long-lived credentials that grant access to production systems or distribution pipelines.
strikes.summary: An attacker stole an access key that Cursor had issued to Fireworks AI following a breach at Fireworks AI, then used it to exfiltrate data from Cursor's read-only systems and trojanize the official Anthropic Claude Code extension on Cursor's extension marketplace. The compromise resulted in a malicious version of the Claude Code extension being distributed to Cursor users.

strikes.title: Attackers Exploit UnrealIRCd Flaw That Enables Server-Level Command Injection
strikes.location: Installations of UnrealIRCd open-source IRC server software; flagged by CISA with active exploitation observed across its jurisdiction.
strikes.data_affected: UnrealIRCd IRC server instances; server-level command execution capability exposed via improper delimiter neutralization flaw.
strikes.impact: Any organization or individual running a vulnerable version of UnrealIRCd is at risk of full server-level command injection. Scale of affected deployments not disclosed in the report, but CISA's KEV listing signals confirmed, broad active exploitation.
strikes.prevention: Apply the vendor-issued patch or upgrade UnrealIRCd to the fixed version immediately, and restrict IRC server port exposure to trusted networks using firewall rules to reduce the attack surface.
strikes.summary: Attackers are actively exploiting CVE-2026-114713, a high-severity (CVSS 8.6) improper neutralization of delimiters vulnerability in UnrealIRCd, an open-source IRC server. CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog in response to confirmed in-the-wild exploitation enabling server-level command injection.

strikes.title: Hackers Exploit PHP2Shell Flaws in Check Point Gateways to Deploy TSGA Backdoor and Wipe ESXi Files
strikes.location: Israeli organizations running Check Point Security Gateways, Israel
strikes.data_affected: Check Point Security Gateway systems running Gaia OS; ESXi virtual machine files (wiped); systems compromised by the TSGA backdoor implant.
strikes.impact: Multiple Israeli organizations were targeted; attackers gained initial access, escalated privileges on Gaia OS, deployed a persistent TSGA backdoor, and destructively wiped ESXi files. The full scope of affected organizations and data loss is not fully disclosed, though a broader follow-up campaign was reported.
strikes.prevention: Apply all available patches to Check Point Security Gateways immediately, specifically those addressing the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities, and enforce strict network segmentation to limit lateral movement and access to ESXi hypervisor management interfaces.
strikes.summary: An unknown threat actor exploited PHP2Shell vulnerabilities in unpatched Check Point Security Gateways, chained with a previously unreported local privilege escalation flaw in Gaia OS, to deploy a backdoor named TSGA and wipe ESXi files. The campaign began on October 30, 2026, and was specifically directed at Israeli organizations, with indications of a broader follow-up operation.

strikes.title: Hackers Exploit N-central Flaws to Infect 21 Servers, Including 19 Running Hotfix 2
strikes.location: N-able N-central managed IT platform servers (customer-deployed instances)
strikes.data_affected: N-central managed IT platform servers; systems and integrations hosted on or managed through the 21 compromised N-central instances
strikes.impact: 21 N-central servers confirmed infected, including 19 running Hotfix 2; N-able was forced to restrict platform features and integrations, disrupting functionality for an undisclosed number of downstream managed service provider (MSP) customers
strikes.prevention: Apply vendor-issued patches and hotfixes to N-central immediately upon release, and restrict internet-exposed management interfaces to trusted IP ranges to limit the attack surface for exploitation of newly disclosed vulnerabilities
strikes.summary: Threat actors exploited two newly disclosed vulnerabilities in N-able's N-central platform, tracked as 4EverAble2Shell and Agent2Shell, to compromise 21 servers, 19 of which were running Hotfix 2. In response, N-able restricted certain N-central features and integrations while remediation was completed.

strikes.title: 186 Fake AI Domains Redirect Users to ClickFix Lures, Browser Malware, and Search Hijackers
strikes.location: Broadly internet-facing; campaign targets global users attempting to reach AI tools via lookalike domains — no single geographic ground zero disclosed.
strikes.data_affected: Browser settings, search configuration, and potentially user credentials or browsing data targeted via hijacking extensions and ClickFix-style malware payloads.
strikes.impact: End users who mistype or are redirected to AI-tool lookalike domains are exposed to browser-hijacking malware and malicious extensions; full victim scale not disclosed, though 186 fraudulent domains are confirmed active in the campaign.
strikes.prevention: Implement DNS filtering and browser-level safe browsing controls to block known lookalike and typosquatting domains before users can land on them, specifically covering AI-tool brand names.
strikes.summary: Cybersecurity researchers uncovered a campaign dubbed "TypoPrompting" in which 186 lookalike domains impersonating popular AI tools serve ClickFix-style lures and browser-hijacking malware to unsuspecting users. Victims who attempt to reach familiar AI applications are instead prompted with fake verification steps that install browser hijackers and search-redirecting extensions.

strikes.title: SCKit Malware Turns ScreenConnect Support Sessions Into Potential MSP Attack Paths
strikes.location: ConnectWise ScreenConnect deployments, primarily targeting MSP environments (vendor headquartered in the United States)
strikes.data_affected: ConnectWise ScreenConnect remote access sessions and potentially downstream MSP-managed endpoints and networks accessible via those sessions.
strikes.impact: MSPs and organizations relying on ConnectWise ScreenConnect for remote support are at risk of full session hijacking and lateral movement into client environments; the scale of affected deployments is not disclosed in the report.
strikes.prevention: Apply the available patch for CVE-2026-84869 in ConnectWise ScreenConnect immediately, and restrict ScreenConnect access to allowlisted IP ranges to prevent unauthorized exploitation of support sessions.
strikes.summary: An ongoing campaign is exploiting a now-patched critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-84869, CVSS 9.9) in ConnectWise ScreenConnect remote access software using a custom attacker toolkit dubbed SCKit. The campaign targets ScreenConnect deployments to hijack support sessions and create attack paths into managed service provider (MSP) environments.

strikes.title: Calendar Invites and Live Proxies: Inside a Google Session Hijacking Campaign
strikes.location: Corporate users globally; campaign infrastructure neutralized by Material Security (US-based).
strikes.data_affected: Live Google session tokens and authenticated corporate user sessions.
strikes.impact: An unspecified number of corporate users across organizations had their active Google sessions hijacked. Hundreds of attacker domains were identified and taken down, indicating a broad-scale, sustained operation; exact victim count and downstream data exposure were not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Enforce hardware-bound session credentials and phishing-resistant MFA (e.g., FIDO2/passkeys) so that stolen session tokens cannot be replayed by an attacker from a different device or network context.
strikes.summary: Since mid-August 2026, a large-scale phishing operation dubbed Operation CloudFire has been harvesting live Google session tokens from corporate users by abusing calendar invites and live proxies. The campaign was engineered to evade standard link-inspection defenses, and Material Security's Threat Research team subsequently took down hundreds of attacker-controlled domains.

strikes.title: Attacker Used 4,837 Hijacked GitHub Accounts to Run a CI Secret Stealer in 1,806+ Repositories
strikes.location: GitHub platform (repositories globally accessible), with the attack originating from hijacked user accounts on GitHub's infrastructure.
strikes.data_affected: CI/CD workflow secrets, cloud credentials, and repository-accessible sensitive environment variables across 1,806+ GitHub repositories.
strikes.impact: At least 1,806 GitHub repositories were compromised across a wide range of organizations and individual developers; cloud credentials and CI secrets from those repositories were likely harvested by the attacker. The full scope of downstream victims is not yet disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Enforce short-lived, scoped CI/CD secrets and rotate all repository and cloud credentials immediately; use GitHub's secret scanning and push-protection features to detect and block credential exposure before pipelines execute.
strikes.summary: An attacker leveraged stolen credentials for 4,837 GitHub accounts to inject a secret-stealing payload into repositories those accounts had write access to. The stealer targeted CI/CD workflow secrets and cloud credentials, successfully executing in at least 1,806 repositories.

strikes.title: ScreenConnect Attacks Target at Least 288 Endpoints Across 48 Organizations With Rogue Clients
strikes.location: Multiple organizations in ConnectWise partner environments, predominantly managed service provider (MSP) customer networks.
strikes.data_affected: Endpoints and systems of victim organizations accessed via unauthorized ScreenConnect remote-access clients; scope of data exfiltration not disclosed.
strikes.impact: At least 288 endpoints across 48 organizations were compromised through rogue remote-management clients, representing a broad multi-tenant intrusion campaign; full operational fallout was not disclosed at time of reporting.
strikes.prevention: Enforce allowlisting of authorized remote-management tools and regularly audit all active ScreenConnect client instances to detect and quarantine rogue or unrecognized installations.
strikes.summary: Threat actors deployed rogue ScreenConnect clients to gain unauthorized access to at least 288 endpoints across 48 organizations. ConnectWise disabled five third-party extensions in partner environments as a precaution, while stating there is no evidence of compromise to its own infrastructure or a vulnerability in ScreenConnect itself.

strikes.title: AntiFox AI Pentesting Platform Linked to Attacks That Accessed AWS Production Secrets
strikes.location: AWS cloud production environments belonging to victim organizations, accessed via Alibaba Cloud-hosted AntiFox interfaces.
strikes.data_affected: AWS production secrets and credentials; compromised cloud environment access tokens and configuration data enabling lateral movement.
strikes.impact: Multiple victim organizations suffered confirmed compromise of their AWS production environments, with attackers achieving lateral movement beyond the initial point of entry. Full scale of affected organizations and downstream damage not disclosed in the report.
strikes.prevention: Enforce least-privilege IAM policies and rotate AWS credentials regularly; implement AWS CloudTrail monitoring with automated alerts for anomalous API calls or access from unexpected geographic regions or cloud providers (e.g., Alibaba Cloud IPs).
strikes.summary: Threat actors abused AntiFox, an emerging agentic AI penetration testing platform, to steal AWS production credentials across multiple confirmed intrusions. The attackers leveraged Alibaba Cloud-hosted AntiFox interfaces to access victims' AWS environments and pivot laterally into compromised infrastructure.

strikes.title: Hackers Target Qlik Sense Servers With Reverse Shells, Stage ActiveMQ and Veeam Exploits
strikes.location: Multiple EU-based customer environments running Qlik Sense servers
strikes.data_affected: Qlik Sense server environments; systems also staged for potential ActiveMQ and Veeam exploitation
strikes.impact: Multiple EU-based organizations were targeted; the reverse shell payloads were not successfully delivered, limiting confirmed operational impact, though the full scope of any parallel ActiveMQ/Veeam staging was not disclosed
strikes.prevention: Patch Qlik Sense servers to the latest available version and enforce application allowlisting and constrained PowerShell language mode on those hosts to prevent unauthorized reverse shell execution
strikes.summary: Threat actors targeted Qlik Sense servers belonging to multiple EU-based organizations in October 2026, attempting to deliver PowerShell reverse shell commands within a window of just over three minutes. Cynet's CyOps and Research teams detected the suspicious activity, which also staged ActiveMQ and Veeam exploits, though the reverse shell attempts were ultimately unsuccessful.

strikes.title: eMudhra Revokes 8 More CAs It Previously Declared Unaffected by Key Compromise
strikes.location: eMudhra, a Certificate Authority headquartered in India
strikes.data_affected: Private keys and intermediate certificate authority (CA) certificates of 8 additional intermediate CAs, used by eMudhra to sign issued certificates.
strikes.impact: 8 more intermediate CAs operated by eMudhra have been revoked, compounding the original October compromise; the full downstream impact on certificates signed by these CAs — and their relying parties — is not fully disclosed in the report.
strikes.prevention: Implement strict code review and automated security testing for any in-house scripts that interact with cryptographic key material, including isolation of CA private key operations from general-purpose scripting environments.
strikes.summary: eMudhra's in-house Python script, responsible for an October key compromise, has led to the revocation of 8 additional intermediate certificate authorities (CAs) that were previously declared unaffected. Although the private keys of these 8 CAs were not cryptographically weakened, a flaw in the same script triggered their revocation, expanding the scope of the original incident.

strikes.title: Railway Says Stolen Customer AI Keys Led to $740,000 in Estimated Unauthorized Usage Charges
strikes.location: Railway (platform-as-a-service provider), United States
strikes.data_affected: Customer-stored secrets including AI provider API keys and database credentials held within the Railway platform.
strikes.impact: Railway customers faced an estimated $740,000 in unauthorized AI usage charges stemming from the misuse of their stolen API keys; Railway has committed to covering those charges where AI providers decline to issue refunds.
strikes.prevention: Encrypt and vault all customer secrets at rest using a dedicated secrets management solution (e.g., HashiCorp Vault) with strict access controls and anomaly-based usage monitoring on API keys to detect and auto-revoke keys exhibiting abnormal spending patterns before losses accumulate.
strikes.summary: In October, threat actors breached Railway, a platform-as-a-service provider, and stole AI API keys that customers had stored on the platform. The stolen keys were then used to generate an estimated $740,000 in unauthorized AI usage charges against those customers.

strikes.title: Cisco BroadWorks and Openwave Flaws Actively Exploited Despite Available Patches
strikes.location: United States and globally — organizations running Cisco BroadWorks and Openwave Messaging Webtop Media Transcoder products.
strikes.data_affected: Cisco BroadWorks platform and Openwave Messaging Webtop Media Transcoder systems; CVE-2026-20320 involves improper restriction of XML external entity (XXE) processing, potentially exposing server-side files and sensitive configuration data.
strikes.impact: Organizations running unpatched Cisco BroadWorks and Openwave Messaging deployments are actively targeted; full scope and number of affected victims not disclosed in the report.
strikes.prevention: Apply the vendor-issued patches for CVE-2026-20320 and the Openwave flaw immediately, as CISA's KEV listing confirms active exploitation and federal agencies are mandated to remediate by the KEV deadline.
strikes.summary: CISA added two actively exploited vulnerabilities — CVE-2026-20320 in Cisco BroadWorks and a flaw in Openwave Messaging Webtop Media Transcoder — to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Despite available patches, threat actors have been confirmed exploiting both flaws in the wild.

strikes.title: SGLang RCE Exploit Breaches NEAR AI, Steals Data From 18 Agents and About 100 Users
strikes.location: NEAR AI inference server (NEAR Protocol / NEAR AI, headquartered in San Francisco, USA)
strikes.data_affected: Inference server requests and associated data from approximately 18 AI agents and ~100 users, including requests processed in confidential/TEE mode.
strikes.impact: NEAR AI's inference infrastructure was compromised; data belonging to roughly 18 agents and approximately 100 users was exposed, with confidential-mode requests — intended to be processed inside a trusted execution environment — potentially viewed by the attacker.
strikes.prevention: Apply security patches or input-validation hardening to the SGLang inference engine promptly, and enforce strict network-level isolation on inference servers to prevent unauthorized remote code execution.
strikes.summary: An attacker exploited a remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in SGLang, an open-source AI inference engine, to execute arbitrary code on one of NEAR AI's inference servers. The attacker was able to access requests being processed on that server, including those sent in confidential mode within a trusted execution environment (TEE).

strikes.title: Binance's Post-Mortem Is Out. The $6.3 Billion Hack Started With a Job Offer.
strikes.location: Ronin Network (Sky Mavis), Vietnam / decentralized bridge infrastructure
strikes.data_affected: Ronin Network validator private keys; crypto assets (ETH and USDC) drained from the Ronin bridge smart contract.
strikes.impact: The Ronin Network bridge — underpinning the Axie Infinity game ecosystem — was drained of hundreds of millions of dollars in crypto assets, making it one of the largest crypto heists on record. Players and liquidity providers on the platform were directly affected; Binance assisted in tracing and partially freezing stolen funds.
strikes.prevention: Enforce strict multi-party authorization (e.g., requiring a supermajority of independent validators for any bridge transaction) so that compromise of a single employee's credentials cannot unilaterally authorize large withdrawals.
strikes.summary: A fraudulent job offer was used to socially engineer an employee, ultimately enabling attackers to compromise the Ronin Network bridge and steal approximately $625 million (reported here as $6.3 billion, likely reflecting peak token valuations) in cryptocurrency. Binance published a post-mortem detailing how the attack began with the fake recruitment approach.

strikes.title: FBI warns ARTEX AI hacking tool is powering global cyberattacks
strikes.location: ConnectWise supply-chain infrastructure, United States (Tampa, FL), with downstream impact on Microsoft 365 customer environments globally.
strikes.data_affected: Microsoft 365 customer environments accessed via the compromised ConnectWise supply-chain; scope of data exfiltrated not disclosed.
strikes.impact: Organizations worldwide using ConnectWise-managed Microsoft 365 environments were affected; exact number of victims and full operational fallout not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Enforce strict third-party vendor access controls and continuous monitoring of privileged integrations (e.g., ConnectWise ScreenConnect/Automate) to detect anomalous lateral movement into downstream Microsoft 365 tenants before compromise propagates.
strikes.summary: Hackers leveraging an AI-powered penetration-testing framework called ARTEX conducted a supply-chain breach of ConnectWise, compromising Microsoft 365 customer environments. The FBI issued a warning attributing the global cyberattack campaign to the automated capabilities of the ARTEX tool.

strikes.title: TSMC employee data breach linked to cloud provider
strikes.location: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), Taiwan, via a third-party cloud provider
strikes.data_affected: Personal employee data (6.9 GB), including details not fully disclosed in the report, exfiltrated from a third-party cloud provider used by TSMC.
strikes.impact: TSMC employees' personal data was exposed; the data was publicly listed for auction by a threat actor. The full scope of affected individuals was not disclosed in the report.
strikes.prevention: Enforce strict third-party vendor security assessments and contractual data-handling requirements, including mandatory encryption-at-rest and regular audits of cloud providers' access controls to prevent supply-chain data exposure.
strikes.summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) confirmed that personal employee data was leaked online after a threat actor listed 6.9 GB of allegedly stolen information for auction. The breach was traced to a cloud provider associated with TSMC rather than TSMC's own systems directly.

strikes.title: Cursor confirms security breach led to malicious Claude Code extension
strikes.location: Cursor's AI code-editor marketplace, United States
strikes.data_affected: Credentials belonging to Fireworks AI; Cursor marketplace extension distribution pipeline; the malicious Claude Code extension delivered to end users.
strikes.impact: Cursor's marketplace and its user base were directly affected, as a trojanized extension was made available through the official channel. The full scope of users who installed the malicious extension was not disclosed in the report.
strikes.prevention: Enforce cryptographic code-signing and independent integrity verification for all marketplace extensions, so that even if publisher credentials are stolen, unsigned or tampered packages are automatically rejected before distribution.
strikes.summary: Cursor confirmed a security breach in which attackers stole credentials from AI infrastructure provider Fireworks AI and used them to publish a malicious Claude Code extension through Cursor's official marketplace. The compromised extension was distributed to Cursor users before the breach was detected and confirmed.

strikes.title: Trezor confirms crypto-stealing implants in three wallets, releases fix
strikes.location: Southeast Asia — via CryptoBilis, a Trezor reseller operating in the region
strikes.data_affected: Cryptocurrency wallet recovery phrases (seed phrases) stored on Trezor Safe 5 hardware wallets
strikes.impact: At least three confirmed compromised devices sold to end customers through the CryptoBilis reseller channel in Southeast Asia; affected users' wallet recovery phrases were at risk of exfiltration, potentially enabling full theft of cryptocurrency holdings. Full scope of financial losses not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Purchase hardware wallets exclusively from the manufacturer's official store or verified authorized resellers, and perform a physical tamper-evidence inspection and firmware integrity check upon receipt before use.
strikes.summary: Trezor confirmed that three Safe 5 hardware wallets sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis contained malicious hardware implants designed to intercept and exfiltrate wallet recovery phrases via cellular networks. Trezor has acknowledged the compromise and released a firmware fix.

strikes.title: German military drone operations disrupted by cyberattack
strikes.location: Quantum Systems, a defense technology company headquartered in Germany
strikes.data_affected: Systems related to military drone operations and defense technology infrastructure at Quantum Systems; specific data or systems compromised not fully disclosed.
strikes.impact: German military drone operations were disrupted; Quantum Systems' operational capabilities were affected. The full scale of the fallout and any data exfiltration were not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Implement network segmentation and strict access controls to isolate operational technology (OT) systems supporting drone operations from general IT infrastructure, limiting attackers' lateral movement in the event of a breach.
strikes.summary: German defense technology company Quantum Systems confirmed it detected a cyberattack by hostile actors in late October that disrupted military drone operations. The incident was identified as an active intrusion, though specific technical details of the attack vector were not fully disclosed.

strikes.title: Check Point gateways hacked via PHP2Shell to deploy VMware ESXi wiper
strikes.location: Organizations running Check Point Security Gateway appliances globally; victim headquarters not disclosed.
strikes.data_affected: VMware ESXi host filesystems and virtual machine data; Check Point Security Gateway management and network access controls.
strikes.impact: Organizations running vulnerable Check Point Security Gateway instances faced destruction of VMware ESXi-hosted virtual machines and data via wiper malware; scale of affected victims not disclosed in the report.
strikes.prevention: Apply all available Check Point Security Gateway patches immediately and restrict external management-plane access to trusted IP ranges to eliminate the exploitable attack surface.
strikes.summary: Vulnerable Check Point Security Gateway appliances were compromised via PHP2Shell attacks, allowing threat actors to deploy data-wiping malware targeting VMware ESXi hosts. The campaign exploited unpatched gateway instances to gain a foothold and execute destructive payloads against virtualization infrastructure.

strikes.title: Check Point warns of zero-day flaw exploited for root access
strikes.location: Check Point Software Technologies — network security appliances deployed at customer sites globally (vendor headquartered in Tel Aviv, Israel).
strikes.data_affected: Root-level access to Check Point security appliances; persistent footholds on vulnerable devices, potentially exposing all data and configurations managed by those systems.
strikes.impact: Organizations running vulnerable Check Point devices were at risk of full device compromise with root-level privileges, enabling attackers to maintain persistent access; the scale of affected victims was not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Apply Check Point's emergency hotfixes immediately to all affected devices, and enforce strict network segmentation to limit management-plane exposure to untrusted networks.
strikes.summary: A high-severity zero-day vulnerability in Check Point Software's network security devices has been actively exploited by threat actors since late October to gain root privileges and establish persistence on affected systems. Check Point issued emergency hotfixes in response to the ongoing exploitation.

strikes.title: Police arrest 354 suspects in dark web cybercrime crackdown
strikes.location: Multiple countries; joint international law enforcement operation with no single disclosed ground-zero country.
strikes.data_affected: Dark web marketplace infrastructure and user/vendor data across Archetyp, Nemesis, Tor2Door, Bohemia, and Kingdom markets; identities of vendors and buyers exposed during the operation.
strikes.impact: 354 suspects arrested globally; five dark web criminal marketplaces disrupted or taken down, impacting an undisclosed number of vendors and buyers who relied on these platforms for illicit trade.
strikes.prevention: Law enforcement agencies should continue sharing intelligence across jurisdictions and monitor cryptocurrency transaction flows to identify and de-anonymize dark web market participants before they can migrate to new platforms.
strikes.summary: International law enforcement authorities arrested 354 suspects in a coordinated operation targeting vendors and buyers operating on five dark web marketplaces: Archetyp, Nemesis, Tor2Door, Bohemia, and Kingdom. The operation dismantled significant criminal infrastructure used for illicit trade across these platforms.

strikes.title: New worm-like 'SCKit' malware targets MSPs in ScreenConnect attacks
strikes.location: Managed service providers (MSPs) and their customer environments globally, exploited via ScreenConnect remote-access software.
strikes.data_affected: MSP technician workstations, ScreenConnect remote-access sessions, and downstream managed customer networks and devices.
strikes.impact: Multiple MSPs and their managed customer environments were targeted; the worm-like propagation mechanism means each compromised MSP technician machine can become a pivot point to infect entire portfolios of client networks. Full scale of affected organizations was not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Immediately apply all available ScreenConnect security patches and restrict technician access using multi-factor authentication (MFA) and least-privilege session controls to limit lateral spread from compromised endpoints.
strikes.summary: A worm-like malware toolkit called SCKit was deployed in attacks against managed service providers (MSPs) by exploiting ScreenConnect remote-access software. The malware is engineered to spread laterally from compromised customer endpoints to MSP technicians' machines, enabling further compromise of additional managed customer networks.

strikes.title: Hackers compromise 4,800 GitHub accounts to steal cloud credentials
strikes.location: GitHub platform (globally hosted by GitHub, Inc., headquartered in San Francisco, California, USA)
strikes.data_affected: Cloud credentials and secrets stored in or accessible from GitHub repositories (e.g., API keys, tokens, and other cloud-service secrets).
strikes.impact: At least 61,764 GitHub repositories were probed and subjected to malicious pull requests; an unknown number of repository owners and cloud service accounts may have had credentials exfiltrated. The full downstream impact on affected cloud environments was not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Enforce mandatory code-review policies and secret-scanning alerts on all repositories, and require signed commits with verified contributor identities to block malicious pull requests from compromised or unrecognized accounts before they are merged.
strikes.summary: A campaign named 'wfx-loot' leveraged 4,837 compromised GitHub accounts to probe 61,764 repositories, open malicious pull requests, and push secrets-stealing malware targeting cloud credentials. The large-scale operation systematically abused GitHub's collaborative features to deliver credential-harvesting payloads across a wide range of projects.

strikes.title: City of Osaka warns of data breach impacting 1 million as Japan reels from dozens of cyber incidents
strikes.location: City of Osaka municipal government, Osaka, Japan
strikes.data_affected: Personal data of approximately 1 million residents, including information sufficient to enable phishing emails spoofing the city government.
strikes.impact: Up to 1 million Osaka residents had their personal data compromised; the city's entire population of 2.8 million was placed on alert for follow-on phishing attempts exploiting the leaked data.
strikes.prevention: Implement strict data minimization and access controls on resident databases, combined with continuous monitoring for unauthorized data exfiltration, to limit exposure in the event of a breach.
strikes.summary: The City of Osaka confirmed a data breach affecting approximately 1 million individuals, prompting officials to warn all 2.8 million residents to be vigilant against suspicious emails impersonating the local government. The incident is one of dozens of cyberattacks reported across Japan in a recent wave.

strikes.title: University of Texas at Arlington warns personal information stolen during cyberattack
strikes.location: University of Texas at Arlington, Arlington, Texas, USA
strikes.data_affected: Personal information of individuals associated with the university; specific data types not disclosed.
strikes.impact: Members of the University of Texas at Arlington community (students, staff, and/or faculty) had personal information stolen; the full scope and number of affected individuals were not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Implement comprehensive data-loss prevention (DLP) controls and network segmentation to limit access to sensitive personal data, reducing the ability of threat actors to exfiltrate it during a breach.
strikes.summary: The University of Texas at Arlington confirmed that personal information was stolen during a cyberattack following an internal investigation. A university spokesperson acknowledged the breach to Recorded Future News but declined to specify what categories of data were exfiltrated.
